components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 汤, 酒; 海 is the sea.
每 (měi) — near sound — 海 is hǎi; 每 also sounds out 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.

example.hanzi: 潜水员在海底发现了一艘沉船。
example.pinyin: Qiánshuǐyuán zài hǎidǐ fāxiàn le yī sōu chénchuán.
example.english: The diver found a sunken ship on the seabed.
example.fact: The Challenger Deep, the lowest known point of the seabed in the Mariana Trench, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below sea level — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with over 2 kilometers to spare. Only a handful of crewed submersibles have ever reached its bottom.

examples.hanzi: 海底有很多五颜六色的鱼。
examples.pinyin: Hǎidǐ yǒu hěn duō wǔyán-liùsè de yú.
examples.english: There are lots of colorful fish on the seabed.

examples.hanzi: 他们要在海底铺一条电缆。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yào zài hǎidǐ pū yì tiáo diànlǎn.
examples.english: They are going to lay a cable on the seabed.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pressing down; also in 压 press, 按 push.
卬 (yǎng) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 仰 yǎng and 迎 yíng.
阝 (city, 右耳旁 on the right) — marks places, as in 都 capital, 邮 mail; the gloomy sense of 郁 is a borrowed one.
有 (yǒu) hints at the sound only loosely.

example.hanzi: 长期的压力可能导致抑郁。
example.pinyin: Chángqī de yālì kěnéng dǎozhì yìyù.
example.english: Long-term stress can lead to depression.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that depression affects more than 280 million people worldwide, making it one of the leading causes of disability globally. Twentieth-century research linking mood to brain chemistry, particularly neurotransmitters like serotonin, helped reshape it from a poorly understood personal weakness into a recognized, treatable medical condition.

examples.hanzi: 他整天闷闷不乐，医生说可能是抑郁。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān mènmèn-bùlè, yīshēng shuō kěnéng shì yìyù.
examples.english: He's gloomy all day, and the doctor says it may be depression.

examples.hanzi: 她因为抑郁一直睡不好觉。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi yìyù yìzhí shuì bù hǎo jiào.
examples.english: She hasn't been able to sleep well because of depression.

components.note: 亻 (person, 单人旁) — marks people and relationships, as in 他 he, 们 plural, 住 live.
至 (zhì) nearly matches zhí, with a different tone; it also sounds out 致 zhì and 室 shì.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 这是我哥哥的女儿,我的侄女。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ gēge de nǚ'ér, wǒ de zhínǚ.
example.english: This is my older brother's daughter, my niece.
example.fact: Genetically, a niece shares on average 25% of her DNA with an aunt or uncle, the same fraction of shared DNA as between a grandparent and grandchild. This comes from standard rules of human relatedness, since each additional generational or lateral step in a family tree roughly halves the expected genetic overlap.

examples.hanzi: 我的侄女今年上小学一年级。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhínǚ jīnnián shàng xiǎoxué yī niánjí.
examples.english: My niece is in first grade this year.

examples.hanzi: 周末我带侄女去公园玩。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ dài zhínǚ qù gōngyuán wán.
examples.english: On the weekend I take my niece to the park.

components.note: 几 (small table) — a low table with legs. As a sound it gives jī to 机 and 肌, and means how many in 几个.
幺 (tiny thread) — the dictionary story is a cord pulled taut in a frame, so 'to lead'; another account sees a bird net. Origin is disputed.
十 (ten) — the lower bar. Reads shuài to lead (率领) and lǜ for rate (效率, 比率). Memory aid: ten threads pulled together as a rate.

example.hanzi: 明天下雨的几率很高。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān xiàyǔ de jǐlǜ hěn gāo.
example.english: The probability of rain tomorrow is high.
example.fact: Modern probability theory traces back to a 1654 exchange of letters between French mathematicians Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat, who were trying to settle a gambling dispute over how to fairly divide the stakes of an unfinished game of chance. Their correspondence laid mathematical foundations still used today in insurance, weather forecasting, and statistics.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试通过的几率不大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì tōngguò de jīlǜ bú dà.
examples.english: The chance of passing this exam isn't high.

examples.hanzi: 中奖的几率只有百万分之一。
examples.pinyin: Zhòngjiǎng de jīlǜ zhǐ yǒu bǎiwàn fēn zhī yī.
examples.english: The odds of winning a prize are only one in a million.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 健 is a strong body.
建 (jiàn) sounds exactly like 健; also in 键 jiàn.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 他每天下班后都去健身房锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān xiàbān hòu dōu qù jiànshēnfáng duànliàn.
example.english: He goes to the gym to exercise every day after work.
example.fact: The word 'gymnasium' comes from the ancient Greek gymnos, meaning 'naked,' because Greek athletes traditionally trained and competed nude. Ancient gymnasiums were also centers of philosophy and education rather than pure exercise — both Plato's Academy and Aristotle's Lyceum were built around gymnasium complexes in Athens.

examples.hanzi: 这家健身房离我家很近。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiànshēnfáng lí wǒ jiā hěn jìn.
examples.english: This gym is very close to my home.

examples.hanzi: 我办了一张健身房的年卡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàn le yì zhāng jiànshēnfáng de niánkǎ.
examples.english: I got an annual membership card for the gym.

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and heat, as in 烧 burn, 灯 lamp, 烟 smoke; 炮 is a cannon or firecracker, as in 鞭炮.
包 (bāo) — close sound: 炮 pào. 包 also sounds out 抱 bào and 跑 pǎo.

example.hanzi: 过年的时候我们放鞭炮。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen fàng biānpào.
example.english: At New Year we set off firecrackers.
example.fact: 炮 gives 鞭炮 (firecrackers), 大炮 (cannon) and 炮弹 (shell). Firecrackers were traditionally lit to scare off evil spirits. The other readings, páo and bāo, are used in cooking.

examples.hanzi: 新年的时候，我们放鞭炮。
examples.pinyin: Xīnnián de shíhou, wǒmen fàng biānpào.
examples.english: At the New Year we set off firecrackers.

examples.hanzi: 战士们守在大炮旁边。
examples.pinyin: Zhànshìmen shǒu zài dàpào pángbiān.
examples.english: The soldiers are standing guard by the cannon.

components.note: 鱼 (fish) — marks fish and seafood, as in 鲜 fresh, 鲨 shark, 鲤 carp; 鲍 is abalone, as in 鲍鱼.
包 (bāo) — close sound: 鲍 bào. 包 also sounds out 抱 bào.

example.hanzi: 他点了一份鲍鱼。
example.pinyin: Tā diǎn le yí fèn bàoyú.
example.english: He ordered a dish of abalone.
example.fact: 鲍鱼 is abalone, a prized banquet seafood. In classical writing 鲍鱼 referred to smelly salted fish, a different dish. 鲍 is also a surname.

examples.hanzi: 他点了一份红烧鲍鱼。
examples.pinyin: Tā diǎn le yí fèn hóngshāo bàoyú.
examples.english: He ordered a portion of braised abalone.

examples.hanzi: 这位是鲍先生，我们的新同事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shì Bào xiānsheng, wǒmen de xīn tóngshì.
examples.english: This is Mr. Bao, our new colleague.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and passing, as in 过, 进, 送; 透 is to pass through.
秀 (xiù) hints at the sound: 透 tòu is close to 诱 yòu and 锈 xiù.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 阳光透过窗户照进了房间。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng tòuguò chuānghù zhàojìn le fángjiān.
example.english: Sunlight passed through the window into the room.
example.fact: Neutrinos are subatomic particles so weakly interacting that trillions of them pass through the human body every second without any effect. Produced in vast numbers by nuclear reactions inside the Sun, they can pass straight through the entire Earth almost undisturbed, which is why detecting them requires enormous underground tanks shielded from other radiation.

examples.hanzi: 月光透过树叶洒在地上。
examples.pinyin: Yuèguāng tòuguò shùyè sǎ zài dì shàng.
examples.english: Moonlight filters through the leaves onto the ground.

examples.hanzi: 我们透过望远镜看星星。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tòuguò wàngyuǎnjìng kàn xīngxing.
examples.english: We look at the stars through a telescope.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 犭 is the animal radical (犬), as in 猫, 狗, 狼; 猜 once meant a suspicious, wary animal.
青 (qīng) — near sound — 猜 is cāi; 青 also sounds out 清, 请, 情 and 晴.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 科学家们对宇宙的起源提出了各种猜想。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen duì yǔzhòu de qǐyuán tíchū le gèzhǒng cāixiǎng.
example.english: Scientists have proposed various conjectures about the origin of the universe.
example.fact: The Goldbach Conjecture, proposed by mathematician Christian Goldbach in 1742, states that every even integer greater than 2 can be written as the sum of two prime numbers. Despite being verified by computer for numbers up to 4 quintillion without a single exception, it remains unproven and is one of the oldest unsolved problems in mathematics.

examples.hanzi: 这只是我的猜想，不一定对。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ de cāixiǎng, bù yídìng duì.
examples.english: This is just my guess and may not be right.

examples.hanzi: 没有证据，一切都只是猜想。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu zhèngjù, yíqiè dōu zhǐshì cāixiǎng.
examples.english: Without evidence, everything is just speculation.

components.note: 贝 (cowrie) — money and value, as in 财, 货, 买: competing for prizes was once tied to offerings and stakes.
马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 他周末喜欢去看赛马。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōumò xǐhuan qù kàn sàimǎ.
example.english: He likes to watch horse racing on weekends.
example.fact: In 1878, photographer Eadweard Muybridge settled a long-running debate about horse locomotion by using a row of cameras with tripwires to capture a galloping horse frame by frame. The images proved that all four hooves do leave the ground at once, a motion too fast for the naked eye to confirm, and the technique helped launch the development of motion pictures.

examples.hanzi: 明天的赛马比赛吸引了很多观众。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān de sàimǎ bǐsài xīyǐn le hěn duō guānzhòng.
examples.english: Tomorrow's horse race has attracted many spectators.

examples.hanzi: 赛马场上人山人海。
examples.pinyin: Sàimǎchǎng shàng rénshān-rénhǎi.
examples.english: The racecourse was packed with people.

components.note: 勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 这个产品的包装非常精美。
example.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn de bāozhuāng fēicháng jīngměi.
example.english: This product's packaging is very exquisite.
example.fact: Corrugated cardboard, the material behind most modern shipping boxes, was patented in England in 1856 — originally as a liner for tall hats, not for packaging at all. It wasn't adapted for shipping boxes until decades later in the United States, where it quickly replaced heavier wooden crates.

examples.hanzi: 礼物的包装要用漂亮的纸。
examples.pinyin: Lǐwù de bāozhuāng yào yòng piàoliang de zhǐ.
examples.english: Gifts should be wrapped in pretty paper.

examples.hanzi: 我们正在包装这批货物。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhèngzài bāozhuāng zhè pī huòwù.
examples.english: We are packing this batch of goods.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 损 is to damage, as in 损失.
员 (yuán) — loose hint — 损 is sǔn.
土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.

example.hanzi: 地震损坏了很多房屋。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn sǔnhuài le hěnduō fángwū.
example.english: The earthquake damaged many houses.
example.fact: The 1960 Great Chilean Earthquake, at magnitude 9.5, remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded by modern instruments. It damaged or destroyed roughly two million homes and triggered a tsunami that caused destruction as far away as Hawaii, Japan, and the Philippines.

examples.hanzi: 我的手机被摔坏了，屏幕损坏得很严重。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi shuāi huài le, píngmù sǔnhuài de hěn yánzhòng.
examples.english: My phone was dropped, and the screen is badly damaged.

examples.hanzi: 暴风雨损坏了公园里的树。
examples.pinyin: Bàofēngyǔ sǔnhuài le gōngyuán lǐ de shù.
examples.english: The storm damaged the trees in the park.

components.note: 马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.
欠 (open mouth, yawn) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow, 欢 happy.
曷 (hé) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 喝 hē and 渴 kě.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 马歇尔将军提出了帮助欧洲重建的计划。
example.pinyin: Mǎxiē'ěr jiāngjūn tíchū le bāngzhù Ōuzhōu chóngjiàn de jìhuà.
example.english: General Marshall proposed a plan to help rebuild Europe.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, officially the European Recovery Program, provided the equivalent of well over 100 billion of today's dollars to rebuild Western European economies after World War II. Its architect, U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall, remains the only career military general ever awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, which he received in 1953.

examples.hanzi: 马歇尔教授今天给我们讲了历史课。
examples.pinyin: Mǎxiē'ěr jiàoshòu jīntiān gěi wǒmen jiǎng le lìshǐ kè.
examples.english: Professor Marshall gave us a history lesson today.

examples.hanzi: 马歇尔住在我家对面。
examples.pinyin: Mǎxiē'ěr zhù zài wǒ jiā duìmiàn.
examples.english: Marshall lives across from my home.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.
木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.

example.hanzi: 警察持枪进入了大楼。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá chíqiāng jìnrù le dàlóu.
example.english: The police entered the building carrying guns.
example.fact: The AK-47, one of the most widely produced firearms in history with an estimated 75 million-plus units made since 1949, was designed by Soviet engineer Mikhail Kalashnikov. He reportedly said late in life that he wished he had invented something that helped farmers instead, like a lawnmower.

examples.hanzi: 保安持枪站在银行门口。
examples.pinyin: Bǎo'ān chíqiāng zhàn zài yínháng ménkǒu.
examples.english: The security guard stood at the bank entrance holding a gun.

examples.hanzi: 持枪的人必须有合法的证件。
examples.pinyin: Chíqiāng de rén bìxū yǒu héfǎ de zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: People who carry guns must have legal permits.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a cat's meow; also in 叫 shout, 喵 meow.
米 (mǐ) gives the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 眯 mī.
口 (mouth) — a cat's meow; also in 叫 shout, 喵 meow.
米 (mǐ) gives the same syllable with a different tone; it also sounds out 眯 mī.

example.hanzi: 小猫咪咪地叫着,想要吃东西。
example.pinyin: Xiǎomāo mīmī de jiào zhe, xiǎng yào chī dōngxi.
example.english: The kitten meowed, wanting something to eat.
example.fact: Adult cats rarely meow at each other; researchers believe the behavior is aimed mainly at humans, reinforced over thousands of years of domestication because it reliably gets a person's attention. Kittens meow at their mothers, but most cats largely stop meowing at other cats once grown.

examples.hanzi: 我家的猫叫咪咪，很爱睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā de māo jiào Mīmi, hěn ài shuìjiào.
examples.english: My cat is called Mimi and loves to sleep.

examples.hanzi: 小猫饿了，咪咪地叫个不停。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo māo è le, mīmī de jiào gè bù tíng.
examples.english: The kitten was hungry and kept meowing.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 会议因为停电而中断了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì yīnwèi tíngdiàn ér zhōngduàn le.
example.english: The meeting was interrupted because of a power outage.
example.fact: In computing, a 'hardware interrupt' is a signal that temporarily halts a processor's current task so it can immediately respond to something more urgent, such as a keystroke or an incoming network packet. Developed in the 1950s, the concept let computers react quickly to real-world events instead of constantly checking for them, and it remains fundamental to how virtually every modern computer operates.

examples.hanzi: 网络突然中断，视频会议停了。
examples.pinyin: Wǎngluò tūrán zhōngduàn, shìpín huìyì tíng le.
examples.english: The network suddenly cut out and the video meeting stopped.

examples.hanzi: 因为下雨，比赛被迫中断。
examples.pinyin: Yīnwèi xià yǔ, bǐsài bèipò zhōngduàn.
examples.english: The game had to be interrupted because of rain.

components.note: 入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 有人入室盗窃了他家的财物。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén rùshì dàoqiè le tā jiā de cáiwù.
example.english: Someone broke into his house and stole his belongings.
example.fact: Studies of residential burglary patterns have found that most break-ins happen during the day rather than at night, when many homes sit empty because occupants are at work or school. The FBI reports that daytime hours, especially between about 10am and 3pm, see disproportionately more residential burglaries than nighttime hours.

examples.hanzi: 小偷是夜里入室行窃的。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu shì yèlǐ rùshì xíngqiè de.
examples.english: The thief broke into the house at night.

examples.hanzi: 入室盗窃案最近有所增加。
examples.pinyin: Rùshì dàoqiè'àn zuìjìn yǒu suǒ zēngjiā.
examples.english: Burglary cases have increased recently.

components.note: 乐 (music, joy) — simplified from 樂, a stringed instrument on a wooden stand. Read yuè "music" or lè "joy".
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国 country, 回 return, 图 map; 园 is a fenced garden.
元 (yuán) sounds exactly like 园; also in 远 yuǎn, 院 yuàn, 完 wán.

example.hanzi: 迪士尼乐园是很多孩子的梦想目的地。
example.pinyin: Díshìní lèyuán shì hěnduō háizi de mèngxiǎng mùdìdì.
example.english: Disneyland is the dream destination for many children.
example.fact: Disneyland in Anaheim, California, opened in 1955 and was designed under Walt Disney's close personal supervision, from groundbreaking to opening day. It remains the only Disney theme park Walt himself oversaw in full, and its early construction budget was famously so tight that he borrowed against his own life insurance policy to help fund it.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们带孩子去游乐园，那儿真是孩子们的乐园。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dài háizi qù yóulèyuán, nàr zhēn shì háizimen de lèyuán.
examples.english: On the weekend we took the kids to the amusement park; it's truly a paradise for kids.

examples.hanzi: 对小狗来说，大草地就是它们的乐园。
examples.pinyin: Duì xiǎogǒu láishuō, dà cǎodì jiù shì tāmen de lèyuán.
examples.english: For puppies, a big meadow is their playground.

components.note: 钅 (metal; traditional 金) — marks metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 锯 is a saw.
居 (jū) — same sound: 锯 jù/jū. 居 also sounds out 据 jù and 剧 jù.

example.hanzi: 他用锯子锯木头。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng jùzi jù mùtou.
example.english: He is sawing wood with a saw.
example.fact: 锯 is both the noun and the verb. 锯齿 (sawtooth), 电锯 (chainsaw) and 拉锯战 ('sawing battle', a seesaw struggle) all use it.

examples.hanzi: 他拿起锯子，开始锯木板。
examples.pinyin: Tā ná qǐ jùzi, kāishǐ jù mùbǎn.
examples.english: He picked up the saw and started sawing the board.

examples.hanzi: 这把锯很锋利，要小心使用。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ jù hěn fēnglì, yào xiǎoxīn shǐyòng.
examples.english: This saw is sharp, so use it carefully.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks diseases and cravings, as in 病 sick, 痛 pain.
隐 (yǐn) gives the exact sound; it also means hidden, like a hidden craving.

example.hanzi: 他抽烟上瘾了。
example.pinyin: Tā chōuyān shàngyǐn le.
example.english: He became addicted to smoking.
example.fact: 瘾 appears in 上瘾 (get hooked), 烟瘾 (nicotine craving), 网瘾 (internet addiction) and 过瘾 ('so satisfying', as in a craving scratched).

examples.hanzi: 他玩游戏玩上瘾了。
examples.pinyin: Tā wán yóuxì wán shàng yǐn le.
examples.english: He has become addicted to playing games.

examples.hanzi: 我今天过足了看电影的瘾。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān guò zú le kàn diànyǐng de yǐn.
examples.english: I got my fill of watching movies today.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — paying to buy back; also in 财 wealth, 买 buy.
卖 (mài) is a stand-in for an older sound; the same part appears in 读 dú and 续 xù.

example.hanzi: 他想把抵押的房子赎回来。
example.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bǎ dǐyā de fángzi shú huílái.
example.english: He wants to redeem the mortgaged house.
example.fact: 赎 is found in 赎回 (buy back), 赎罪 (atone) and 救赎 (redemption; the film The Shawshank Redemption is 肖申克的救赎).

examples.hanzi: 警察帮他把孩子赎了回来。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá bāng tā bǎ háizi shú le huílái.
examples.english: The police helped him get his child back from the kidnappers.

examples.hanzi: 他想赎罪，所以去做了志愿者。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng shúzuì, suǒyǐ qù zuò le zhìyuànzhě.
examples.english: He wants to atone for his wrongs, so he became a volunteer.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 土壤中缺乏加里会影响植物生长。
example.pinyin: Tǔrǎng zhōng quēfá jiālǐ huì yǐngxiǎng zhíwù shēngzhǎng.
example.english: A lack of potassium in the soil affects plant growth.
example.fact: Potassium is the seventh most abundant element in Earth's crust and is essential for plant growth and human nerve and muscle function. Bananas are often cited as a top potassium source, though foods like potatoes, white beans, and spinach actually contain more potassium per serving.

examples.hanzi: 加里是我大学时的室友。
examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ shì wǒ dàxué shí de shìyǒu.
examples.english: Gary was my roommate in college.

examples.hanzi: 加里每天晚上都去图书馆。
examples.pinyin: Jiālǐ měi tiān wǎnshang dōu qù túshūguǎn.
examples.english: Gary goes to the library every evening.

components.note: 土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.
扌 (hand) — hand radical for actions — 掉 is to drop or lose hold.

example.hanzi: 编辑建议我去掉这段多余的描述。
example.pinyin: Biānjí jiànyì wǒ qùdiào zhè duàn duōyú de miáoshù.
example.english: The editor suggested I remove this redundant passage.
example.fact: CRISPR-Cas9 works like a pair of molecular scissors that can precisely cut out, or remove, a targeted sequence of DNA. The technique, developed by Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier, earned them the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

examples.hanzi: 请把名字前面的称呼去掉。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi qiánmiàn de chēnghu qùdiào.
examples.english: Please remove the title in front of the name.

examples.hanzi: 这个菜去掉辣椒会更好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cài qùdiào làjiāo huì gèng hǎochī.
examples.english: This dish will taste better without the chili.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.
氵 (water) — water and mixing liquids, as in 河, 海, 清: 混 is to mix or muddy.
昆 (kūn) is a close sound clue for hùn; 昆 also in 棍 gùn.

example.hanzi: 他整天在外面鬼混,不好好学习。
example.pinyin: Tā zhěngtiān zài wàimiàn guǐhùn, bù hǎohǎo xuéxí.
example.english: He fools around outside all day instead of studying properly.
example.fact: The three-toed sloth spends up to 15 to 20 hours a day resting in trees and moves so slowly that algae grows directly on its fur, giving it a greenish camouflage. It is one of the most extreme low-energy lifestyles documented among mammals.

examples.hanzi: 他不想再跟那些人鬼混了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng zài gēn nàxiē rén guǐhùn le.
examples.english: He doesn't want to hang around with those people any more.

examples.hanzi: 你别整晚在网吧鬼混，明天还要上班。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié zhěng wǎn zài wǎngbā guǐhùn, míngtiān hái yào shàngbān.
examples.english: Don't mess around at the internet café all night; you have work tomorrow.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.
心 (heart) — wishes and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 愿 is what the heart wants.
原 (yuán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; 原 also in 源 yuán.

example.hanzi: 她情愿一个人旅行,也不愿意跟团。
example.pinyin: Tā qíngyuàn yí gè rén lǚxíng, yě bú yuànyì gēn tuán.
example.english: She would rather travel alone than join a tour group.
example.fact: In 1978, Japanese explorer Naomi Uemura became the first person to reach the North Pole alone, traveling by dog sled from Ellesmere Island. A decade earlier, he had also completed a solo raft descent of the Amazon River, part of a career built around solitary expeditions.

examples.hanzi: 我情愿走路，也不想挤地铁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qíngyuàn zǒulù, yě bù xiǎng jǐ dìtiě.
examples.english: I'd rather walk than squeeze onto the subway.

examples.hanzi: 他情愿吃亏，也不愿跟朋友吵架。
examples.pinyin: Tā qíngyuàn chīkuī, yě bú yuàn gēn péngyou chǎojià.
examples.english: He'd rather lose out than quarrel with a friend.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱; 担 is to carry on the shoulder, then to bear a duty.
旦 (dàn) is a close sound clue for dān; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 胆 dǎn.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.

example.hanzi: 银行要求有人担保才能批准贷款。
example.pinyin: Yínháng yāoqiú yǒurén dānbǎo cái néng pīzhǔn dàikuǎn.
example.english: The bank requires someone to guarantee the loan before it can be approved.
example.fact: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, founded in Siena, Italy, in 1472, is the world's oldest continuously operating bank. It originally issued loans against pawned goods as collateral, an early form of a guaranteed loan.

examples.hanzi: 我可以为他担保，他是个诚实的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ wèi tā dānbǎo, tā shì gè chéngshí de rén.
examples.english: I can vouch for him; he is an honest person.

examples.hanzi: 这台冰箱有三年的担保期。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái bīngxiāng yǒu sān nián de dānbǎoqī.
examples.english: This refrigerator has a three-year guarantee.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.

example.hanzi: 这块场地将用于建设新体育馆。
example.pinyin: Zhè kuài chǎngdì jiāng yòng yú jiànshè xīn tǐyùguǎn.
example.english: This site will be used to build a new stadium.
example.fact: The Panathenaic Stadium in Athens, rebuilt for the first modern Olympics in 1896, sits on the same site as an ancient Greek stadium from the 4th century BC. It is made almost entirely of white marble.

examples.hanzi: 这个场地可以容纳五百人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chǎngdì kěyǐ róngnà wǔbǎi rén.
examples.english: This venue can hold five hundred people.

examples.hanzi: 比赛的场地离地铁站很近。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài de chǎngdì lí dìtiězhàn hěn jìn.
examples.english: The competition venue is very close to the subway station.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water and liquids, as in 海, 汤, 酒; 液 is a liquid.
夜 (yè) — same sound — 液 is yè, like 夜 night.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 水在常温下是液体,加热后会变成气体。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ zài chángwēn xià shì yètǐ, jiārè hòu huì biànchéng qìtǐ.
example.english: Water is a liquid at room temperature and turns into a gas when heated.
example.fact: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at standard room temperature, remaining fluid down to about -39°C. That property is why it was historically used in thermometers and barometers, before health concerns led to its phase-out.

examples.hanzi: 牛奶是一种白色的液体。
examples.pinyin: Niúnǎi shì yì zhǒng báisè de yètǐ.
examples.english: Milk is a kind of white liquid.

examples.hanzi: 实验室里的液体不能随便喝。
examples.pinyin: Shíyànshì lǐ de yètǐ bù néng suíbiàn hē.
examples.english: You must not drink the liquids in the lab casually.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.
⺮ (bamboo, 竹字头) — written things and bamboo goods: 笔 pen, 第 order, 筷 chopsticks; 答 comes from bamboo slips used for replies.
合 (hé, together) — matching an answer to a question; sound is only loose, but 合 also sounds out 搭 dā.

example.hanzi: 他决心努力工作来报答父母的养育之恩。
example.pinyin: Tā juéxīn nǔlì gōngzuò lái bàodá fùmǔ de yǎngyù zhī ēn.
example.english: He resolved to work hard to repay his parents for raising him.
example.fact: Vampire bats are one of the few mammals known to reciprocate favors: a bat that shares regurgitated blood with a hungry roost-mate is more likely to receive blood in return later. This was documented as a real-world example of reciprocal altruism by biologist Gerald Wilkinson in the 1980s.

examples.hanzi: 我永远不会忘记要报答你的恩情。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒngyuǎn bú huì wàngjì yào bàodá nǐ de ēnqíng.
examples.english: I will never forget to repay your kindness.

examples.hanzi: 他用优异的成绩报答老师的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng yōuyì de chéngjì bàodá lǎoshī de bāngzhù.
examples.english: He repaid his teacher's help with excellent grades.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) with 月 — the shady side of a hill, the opposite of 阳 (阝 with 日, sunny); yīn is the dark principle.
艹 (grass) — plants; 茎 is a stem, as in 草 grass, 花 flower. The right part also sounds out 经 jīng and 径 jìng.

example.hanzi: 医生解释了阴茎的基本解剖结构。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiěshì le yīnjīng de jīběn jiěpōu jiégòu.
example.english: The doctor explained the basic anatomy of the penis.
example.fact: Relative to body size, the acorn barnacle has one of the longest penises in the animal kingdom, capable of extending several times its own body length to reach mates in neighboring shells. This is necessary because barnacles are immobile once they settle onto a surface.

examples.hanzi: 医学文章里介绍了阴茎的功能。
examples.pinyin: Yīxué wénzhāng lǐ jièshào le yīnjīng de gōngnéng.
examples.english: The medical article describes the function of the penis.

examples.hanzi: 医学课本里有阴茎的结构图。
examples.pinyin: Yīxué kèběn lǐ yǒu yīnjīng de jiégòutú.
examples.english: The medical textbook has a diagram of the structure of the penis.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
寸 (hand, inch) — traditional 導 had 道 (road) plus 寸 (hand): a hand leading along a road; 道 dào is also a near-sound clue for 导 dǎo.

example.hanzi: 老师的教导让我终身受益。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī de jiàodǎo ràng wǒ zhōngshēn shòuyì.
example.english: My teacher's instruction benefited me for my whole life.
example.fact: Aristotle tutored a young Alexander the Great for several years at the Macedonian court, instructing him in logic, medicine, and rhetoric. Alexander went on to build an empire stretching from Greece to India.

examples.hanzi: 父母的教导，我一直记在心里。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ de jiàodǎo, wǒ yìzhí jì zài xīn lǐ.
examples.english: I have always kept my parents' guidance in mind.

examples.hanzi: 老师耐心地教导每一个学生。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī nàixīn de jiàodǎo měi yí gè xuésheng.
examples.english: The teacher patiently instructs every student.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.

example.hanzi: 王室成员享有许多普通人没有的特权。
example.pinyin: Wángshì chéngyuán xiǎngyǒu xǔduō pǔtōngrén méiyǒu de tèquán.
example.english: Members of the royal family enjoy many privileges that ordinary people do not have.
example.fact: Diplomatic immunity, formalized in the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, grants foreign diplomats privileges such as exemption from local prosecution and taxation. The practice has roots going back to ancient protections for royal envoys.

examples.hanzi: 学生也不应该有特权。
examples.pinyin: Xuésheng yě bù yīnggāi yǒu tèquán.
examples.english: Students should not have special privileges either.

examples.hanzi: 会员享有优先入场的特权。
examples.pinyin: Huìyuán xiǎngyǒu yōuxiān rùchǎng de tèquán.
examples.english: Members enjoy the privilege of priority admission.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
龙 — a picture of a dragon, simplified from 龍. It also sounds out 聋 lóng, 笼 lóng and 拢 lǒng.

example.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了一只巨大的恐龙化石。
example.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchū le yì zhī jùdà de kǒnglóng huàshí.
example.english: The museum displayed a huge dinosaur fossil.
example.fact: The largest dinosaur fossils belong to titanosaurs like Argentinosaurus, estimated to have weighed up to 90 tons and stretched over 30 meters long. That is roughly the length of three school buses end to end.

examples.hanzi: 恐龙在六千多万年前就灭绝了。
examples.pinyin: Kǒnglóng zài liùqiān duō wàn nián qián jiù mièjué le.
examples.english: Dinosaurs went extinct more than sixty million years ago.

examples.hanzi: 我儿子最喜欢的玩具是恐龙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ érzi zuì xǐhuan de wánjù shì kǒnglóng.
examples.english: My son's favorite toy is a dinosaur.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
力 (strength) — 力 marks strength and effort, as in 办, 动, 努, 助; 勇 is strength in action, courage.
甬 (yǒng) — same sound — 勇 is yǒng, like 甬; 甬 also sounds out 通 tōng, 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng.

example.hanzi: 消防员英勇地冲进火场救人。
example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán yīngyǒng de chōngjìn huǒchǎng jiùrén.
example.english: The firefighters heroically rushed into the fire to save people.
example.fact: During the 1966 Aberfan disaster in Wales, rescuers, including off-duty miners, dug through a collapsed coal-waste tip by hand for days trying to reach trapped villagers. The tragedy led to major changes in UK mine safety regulation.

examples.hanzi: 战士们英勇作战，保卫了家园。
examples.pinyin: Zhànshìmen yīngyǒng zuòzhàn, bǎowèi le jiāyuán.
examples.english: The soldiers fought bravely and defended their homeland.

examples.hanzi: 他的英勇行为受到了大家的称赞。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yīngyǒng xíngwéi shòudào le dàjiā de chēngzàn.
examples.english: His heroic act was praised by everyone.

components.note: 木 (wood) — a wooden stick; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
昆 (kūn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 混 hùn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 他用一根棍子把苹果从树上打下来。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng yī gēn gùnzi bǎ píngguǒ cóng shù shàng dǎ xiàlái.
example.english: He used a stick to knock apples down from the tree.
example.fact: Chimpanzees in Gombe National Park, first documented by Jane Goodall in 1960, strip leaves from twigs to fashion simple tools used to fish termites out of their mounds. It is one of the earliest confirmed examples of tool use by a non-human animal.

examples.hanzi: 这根棍子太细了，撑不住他的体重。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gēn gùnzi tài xì le, chēng bu zhù tā de tǐzhòng.
examples.english: This stick is too thin to hold his weight.

examples.hanzi: 老爷爷拄着一根棍子慢慢走路。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo yéye zhǔzhe yì gēn gùnzi mànmàn zǒulù.
examples.english: The old man walks slowly, leaning on a stick.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魂, 魅, 愧; 魔 is a demon.
麻 (má) is a near sound match for mó; also in 磨 mó and 摩 mó.
術 (traditional) — 行 (road) plus 朮 (zhú) as sound: art, method. 术 is the sound part alone; same sound in 述 shù, as in 手术, 技术, 艺术.
师 (shī) is a sound clue for 狮 shī (lion) and 筛 shāi; as a word it means master or teacher.

example.hanzi: 那位魔术师的表演让观众目瞪口呆。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi móshùshī de biǎoyǎn ràng guānzhòng mùdèngkǒudāi.
example.english: That magician's performance left the audience astonished.
example.fact: Harry Houdini, born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874, built his reputation on escape acts, such as freeing himself from locked, water-filled milk cans. He spent his later career debunking fraudulent spiritualists who claimed to contact the dead.

examples.hanzi: 魔术师从帽子里变出了一只兔子。
examples.pinyin: Móshùshī cóng màozi lǐ biàn chū le yì zhī tùzi.
examples.english: The magician pulled a rabbit out of a hat.

examples.hanzi: 我想长大后当一名魔术师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zhǎng dà hòu dāng yì míng móshùshī.
examples.english: I want to become a magician when I grow up.

meanings: (of number, time, size etc) just right

components.note: 忄 (heart) — a fitting feeling; also in 快 happy, 情 feeling.
合 (hé) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 洽 qià, as in 洽谈.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 我到车站的时候,恰好赶上了末班车。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dào chēzhàn de shíhòu, qiàhǎo gǎn shàng le mòbānchē.
example.english: When I arrived at the station, I happened to catch the last bus just in time.
example.fact: Leap seconds are occasionally added to Coordinated Universal Time to keep clocks in sync with Earth's slightly irregular rotation. This ensures that global timekeeping stays just right relative to the actual length of a day.

examples.hanzi: 我刚进门，电话恰好响了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gāng jìn mén, diànhuà qiàhǎo xiǎng le.
examples.english: The phone happened to ring just as I walked in.

examples.hanzi: 这双鞋的大小恰好合适。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié de dàxiǎo qiàhǎo héshì.
examples.english: The size of these shoes is just right.

components.note: 米 (rice) — a picture of grains of rice divided by a line; as a radical it marks grain foods, as in 粉 powder, 粮 grain, 糖 sugar.
欠 (open mouth, yawn) — breath and mouth actions, as in 歌 song, 吹 blow, 欢 happy.
曷 (hé) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 喝 hē and 渴 kě.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 米歇尔是这次会议的主讲人。
example.pinyin: Mǐxiē'ěr shì zhè cì huìyì de zhǔjiǎngrén.
example.english: Michel is the keynote speaker at this conference.
example.fact: U.S. Senator George Mitchell chaired the multi-party talks that produced the 1998 Good Friday Agreement. The agreement largely ended three decades of sectarian violence known as the Troubles in Northern Ireland.

examples.hanzi: 米歇尔在一家银行工作。
examples.pinyin: Mǐxiē'ěr zài yì jiā yínháng gōngzuò.
examples.english: Michelle works at a bank.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天碰到了米歇尔，她还问起你。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān pèngdào le Mǐxiē'ěr, tā hái wènqǐ nǐ.
examples.english: I ran into Michelle yesterday, and she asked about you.

components.note: 甘 (sweet) — marks sweetness, as in 甘 itself and 某; 甜 pairs it with 舌 tongue: sweet to the tongue.
舌 (tongue) — the organ that tastes, as in 话 and 活.
羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.

example.hanzi: 她笑起来的样子很甜美。
example.pinyin: Tā xiào qǐlái de yàngzi hěn tiánměi.
example.english: Her smile looks very sweet.
example.fact: Honey is one of the few foods that essentially never spoils, because its low moisture content and high acidity create an environment hostile to bacteria. Archaeologists have found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs more than 3,000 years old that was reportedly still edible.

examples.hanzi: 这个小女孩有一副甜美的嗓音。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎo nǚhái yǒu yí fù tiánměi de sǎngyīn.
examples.english: This little girl has a sweet voice.

examples.hanzi: 昨晚我做了一个甜美的梦。
examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn wǒ zuò le yí gè tiánměi de mèng.
examples.english: I had a sweet dream last night.

components.note: 犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 在这个国家,乱扔垃圾也算犯法。
example.pinyin: Zài zhège guójiā, luàn rēng lājī yě suàn fànfǎ.
example.english: In this country, littering is also considered breaking the law.
example.fact: Singapore enforces some of the world's strictest anti-littering laws, with fines that can exceed 2,000 Singapore dollars for repeat offenders. Repeat offenders can also be handed mandatory Corrective Work Orders that require them to clean public spaces in reflective vests.

examples.hanzi: 闯红灯是犯法的。
examples.pinyin: Chuǎng hóngdēng shì fànfǎ de.
examples.english: Running a red light is against the law.

examples.hanzi: 你这样做可是犯法，会被警察抓的。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng zuò kěshì fànfǎ, huì bèi jǐngchá zhuā de.
examples.english: What you're doing is illegal, and the police will arrest you.

components.note: 番 (fān) — a turn, to take turns; as a part it sounds out 翻 fān, 潘 pān and 播 bō.

example.hanzi: 他下了一番功夫。
example.pinyin: Tā xià le yì fān gōngfu.
example.english: He put in a good deal of effort.
example.fact: 番 is a measure word for efforts and occasions: 一番话, 三番五次 (repeatedly). It originally meant 'foreign', as in 番茄 (tomato) and 番薯 (sweet potato).

examples.hanzi: 他想了一番，还是决定去。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng le yì fān, háishi juédìng qù.
examples.english: He thought it over and still decided to go.

examples.hanzi: 我们把房间重新整理了一番。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ fángjiān chóngxīn zhěnglǐ le yì fān.
examples.english: We tidied up the room once more.

components.note: 米 (rice) — marks grain and rice, as in 粥 congee, 糖 sugar, 粉 powder; 粒 is a grain, used for small round things.
立 (lì) — same sound: 粒 lì. 立 also sounds out 笠 lì.

example.hanzi: 他碗里剩了几粒米饭。
example.pinyin: Tā wǎn lǐ shèng le jǐ lì mǐfàn.
example.english: A few grains of rice are left in his bowl.
example.fact: 粒 is a measure word for small round things: 一粒米, 一粒糖, 一粒药. It's in 颗粒 (granule) and 粒子 (particle in physics).

examples.hanzi: 盘子里有几粒花生米。
examples.pinyin: Pánzi lǐ yǒu jǐ lì huāshēngmǐ.
examples.english: There are a few peanuts on the plate.

examples.hanzi: 沙粒进了我的鞋子。
examples.pinyin: Shālì jìn le wǒ de xiézi.
examples.english: Sand grains got into my shoes.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 力 is strength, as in 办, 动, 努; 势 is force or momentum.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.hanzi: 这个家族在当地拥有很大的势力。
example.pinyin: Zhège jiāzú zài dāngdì yǒngyǒu hěn dà de shìli.
example.english: This family holds great power and influence in the local area.
example.fact: The Medici family, through control of banking in 15th-century Florence, wielded such immense political influence that four Medici men became popes. The family effectively ruled the Florentine Republic for generations without holding an official hereditary title.

examples.hanzi: 这个组织在当地的势力越来越大。
examples.pinyin: Zhège zǔzhī zài dāngdì de shìlì yuèláiyuè dà.
examples.english: This organization's influence in the area keeps growing.

examples.hanzi: 两家公司在市场上的势力差不多。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng jiā gōngsī zài shìchǎng shàng de shìlì chàbuduō.
examples.english: The two companies have about equal power in the market.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.

example.hanzi: 这项新技术还没有得到官方认可。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng xīn jìshù hái méiyǒu dédào guānfāng rènkě.
example.english: This new technology has not yet received official approval.
example.fact: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's approval process for a new drug typically takes over a decade and can cost more than a billion dollars. It covers multiple phases of clinical trials before the agency grants official approval for public use.

examples.hanzi: 他的工作得到了领导的认可。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gōngzuò dédào le lǐngdǎo de rènkě.
examples.english: His work has been recognized by his superiors.

examples.hanzi: 我认可你的看法，咱们就这么办吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ rènkě nǐ de kànfǎ, zánmen jiù zhème bàn ba.
examples.english: I agree with your view; let's do it that way.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.hanzi: 请在表格上填写您的永久住所地址。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài biǎogé shàng tiánxiě nín de yǒngjiǔ zhùsuǒ dìzhǐ.
example.english: Please fill in your permanent residence address on the form.
example.fact: Çatalhöyük, a Neolithic settlement in modern-day Turkey dating to around 7500 BC, housed thousands of people in densely packed mudbrick residences with no streets between them. Residents entered their homes through holes in the roof.

examples.hanzi: 他的住所离公司只有十分钟路程。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhùsuǒ lí gōngsī zhǐyǒu shí fēnzhōng lùchéng.
examples.english: His residence is only ten minutes from the company.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家的住所现在是一座博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā de zhùsuǒ xiànzài shì yí zuò bówùguǎn.
examples.english: This writer's former residence is now a museum.

components.note: 求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.
力 (strength) — effort, as in 办, 男, 努; 助 is to lend strength.
且 (qiě) is a loose sound clue for zhù; 且 also sounds out 祖 zǔ, 租 zū and 姐 jiě.

example.hanzi: 遇到困难时,不要害怕向别人求助。
example.pinyin: Yùdào kùnnán shí, búyào hàipà xiàng biérén qiúzhù.
example.english: When facing difficulties, don't be afraid to seek help from others.
example.fact: The distress signal SOS, adopted internationally in 1906, was chosen not as an acronym but because its Morse code pattern of three dots, three dashes, three dots is simple and unmistakable to transmit and recognize under pressure.

examples.hanzi: 他向邻居求助，借了一把梯子。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng línjū qiúzhù, jiè le yì bǎ tīzi.
examples.english: He asked his neighbor for help and borrowed a ladder.

examples.hanzi: 如果迷路了，可以向警察求助。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ mílù le, kěyǐ xiàng jǐngchá qiúzhù.
examples.english: If you get lost, you can ask the police for help.

components.note: 至 (zhì) — same sound — 致 is zhì, like 至 (to arrive); 致 is to cause to arrive, then to bring about.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action performed, as in 教, 放, 收.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放; 敬 is respectful behaviour, as in 尊敬.
苟 (gǒu) — sound clue is weak — 敬 is jìng, but 敬 sounds out 警 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 士兵们向国旗致敬。
example.pinyin: Shìbīngmen xiàng guóqí zhìjìng.
example.english: The soldiers saluted the national flag.
example.fact: The military hand salute is thought by some historians to descend from medieval knights raising their visors to show their face and peaceful intent, though the exact origin is debated among historians.

examples.hanzi: 让我们举杯，向老师致敬。
examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒmen jǔbēi, xiàng lǎoshī zhìjìng.
examples.english: Let's raise our glasses and pay tribute to our teacher.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影是向经典老片致敬的作品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng shì xiàng jīngdiǎn lǎopiàn zhìjìng de zuòpǐn.
examples.english: This film is a tribute to classic old movies.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — stretching out by hand; also in 拉 pull, 推 push.
广 (guǎng, wide) gives a rough sound and the idea of broad; the traditional 擴 used 廣.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 公司计划扩大在海外的业务。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī jìhuà kuòdà zài hǎiwài de yèwù.
example.english: The company plans to expand its overseas business.
example.fact: In 1929, astronomer Edwin Hubble observed that distant galaxies are moving away from us at speeds proportional to their distance. This provided key evidence that the universe itself is continuously expanding.

examples.hanzi: 政府决定扩大这条马路的宽度。
examples.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ juédìng kuòdà zhè tiáo mǎlù de kuāndù.
examples.english: The government decided to widen this road.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅想扩大营业面积。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng xiǎng kuòdà yíngyè miànjī.
examples.english: This restaurant wants to expand its floor space.

components.note: 你 (nǐ, you) — the base word; adding 心 makes it the polite form.
心 (heart) — respect from the heart; also in 想 think, 爱 love.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.hanzi: 您好,请问有什么可以帮您的吗?
example.pinyin: Nínhǎo, qǐngwèn yǒu shénme kěyǐ bāng nín de ma?
example.english: Hello, how may I help you?
example.fact: In traditional Japanese business etiquette, the depth and duration of a bow used in greeting varies by rank and occasion. A 45-degree bow called saikeirei is reserved for the deepest apologies or greatest respect, while a much shallower bow suffices for everyday greetings.

examples.hanzi: 您好，我是新来的邻居。
examples.pinyin: Nín hǎo, wǒ shì xīn lái de línjū.
examples.english: Hello, I'm the new neighbor.

examples.hanzi: 您好！请问李经理在吗？
examples.pinyin: Nín hǎo! Qǐngwèn Lǐ jīnglǐ zài ma?
examples.english: Hello! Is Manager Li in?

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — the outer box, as in 国 country and 回. The dictionary reading: four walls of a room, with a child (儿) inside; memory aid only, sound-borrowed.
儿 (legs/child) — inside the box, as in 先 and 兄. Memory aid: the shape is simply a box with two legs; it does not explain 'four'.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.

example.hanzi: 厨师把披萨四分,分给四个孩子。
example.pinyin: Chúshī bǎ pīsà sìfēn, fēn gěi sì gè háizi.
example.english: The chef divided the pizza into four parts, giving one to each of four children.
example.fact: American football games are divided into four 15-minute quarters, a structural choice inherited from early 20th-century college football rules. The setup gave teams scheduled breaks for strategy and rest.

examples.hanzi: 这块蛋糕要四分给我们几个人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài dàngāo yào sì fēn gěi wǒmen jǐ gè rén.
examples.english: This cake is to be cut into four parts for the four of us.

examples.hanzi: 这个苹果要四分，大家都有份。
examples.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ yào sì fēn, dàjiā dōu yǒu fèn.
examples.english: This apple is to be quartered so everyone gets a share.
